descriptionChirho: The outer bodily covering of a human being, especially in contexts of disease (Leviticus skin afflictions), suffering (Job, Lamentations), or physical description.
The skin of an animal, either freshly removed (as in sacrificial procedures, e.g., the skin of the burnt offering) or referring to an animal's outer covering.
Animal skin processed into leather, used for garments, vessels, or other manufactured objects, especially in Levitical purity regulations for leather articles.
